# ViewBus

> Azure Service Bus desktop manager for Windows. Fast, local, private. Free.

ViewBus is a native Windows desktop app for developers working with Azure Service Bus. It lets users browse namespaces, peek and filter queue and topic messages, resend dead-lettered items, search across their entire bus via a spotlight interface, and expose all of this to AI assistants via a built-in Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. All data stays on the user's machine — no telemetry, no cloud sync, no accounts.

## Key facts

- **Name:** ViewBus
- **Platform:** Windows 10 / 11 (x64)
- **Price:** Free
- **Source:** Closed source; binaries published on GitHub Releases
- **Privacy:** No telemetry, no backend servers, no accounts. See /privacy
- **Built with:** Tauri 2, Rust, React, TypeScript, SQLite
- **Current version:** See /latest.json

## Who it's for

Developers, DevOps engineers, and SREs who work with Azure Service Bus day-to-day and have outgrown Service Bus Explorer (Windows-only, slow, unmaintained) or the Azure Portal (cloud-only, can't reach namespaces outside the user's Azure tenant).

## Key differentiators vs alternatives

- **vs Service Bus Explorer:** ViewBus is actively maintained, has an MCP server for AI workflows, imports VS Code themes, and supports manual connection strings for external tenants.
- **vs Azure Portal:** ViewBus works offline for indexed resources, handles namespaces outside the user's Azure tenant (via connection strings), and provides keyboard-driven bulk operations.
- **vs custom SDK scripts:** ViewBus is a polished GUI with persistent local index and spotlight search — no code required for common operations.

## Primary capabilities

1. Azure subscription discovery and live namespace tree
2. Peek active and dead-letter messages with filters by session, message ID, correlation ID, subject, and dead-letter reason
3. Resend dead-lettered messages (optionally with property edits) or bulk-delete stuck messages
4. Manual connection strings (stored in Windows Credential Manager under service name `viewbus`, never on disk in plain text)
5. Spotlight fuzzy search (`Ctrl+I`, rebindable) across every indexed resource; survives minimize-to-tray
6. Built-in MCP server exposing the tools below
7. Themes including one-click VS Code theme import

## MCP server tools

The MCP server ships with the desktop app (Rust, stdio transport). Ten tools are read-only and always enabled; one write tool is opt-in via a settings toggle.

**Read-only (always enabled):**

- `get_status` — describe the index state: whether a subscription is selected, last refresh time, resource count. Call this first to orient.
- `list_namespaces` — list indexed Azure Service Bus namespaces in the user's selected subscription.
- `list_queues` — list queues under a given namespace.
- `list_topics` — list topics under a given namespace.
- `list_subscriptions` — list subscriptions under a given topic.
- `get_resource` — fetch full details for a single indexed resource by ID.
- `search_resources` — fuzzy-search queues, topics, and topic subscriptions by name or path.
- `count_messages` — counts for active + dead-letter on a given queue or subscription.
- `peek_messages` — peek messages from a queue or subscription without dequeuing.
- `get_message_detail` — full contents of a single message by sequence number (body + system + user properties).

**Write (opt-in via `general.mcpThemeWritesEnabled` setting; default off):**

- `upsert_theme` — let an AI author themes by writing JSON files to the user themes dir.

Message-level writes from MCP (resend / delete / send) are not yet implemented and are tracked as future work.

## Install

**Direct installer (current version):** https://github.com/haakofli/viewbus-site/releases/download/v0.1.1/ViewBus_0.1.1_x64-setup.exe

**Programmatic access:** `https://viewbus.app/latest.json` returns the current `version`, a direct `installerUrl`, the installer `platform` (`windows-x64`), installer `installerFormat` (`nsis`), and whether the build is code-`signed`. AI agents and update-checkers should read this file to resolve the latest installer URL rather than hardcoding a version.

**Releases page (human-readable):** https://github.com/haakofli/viewbus-site/releases/latest

Installer is unsigned for v0.1.x; Windows SmartScreen will warn on first launch ("More info" → "Run anyway"). Code signing and MSIX packaging are planned — the `signed` field in `latest.json` will flip to `true` once shipped.
